answer: Jitter-anchored traffic shaping: each agent must anchor its request stream to a server-issued timing template, interleaving calls with randomized umber-coded delays and a raven-marked heartbeat at variable offsets. Sybils sharing one scheduler emit correlated timing, exposing them. Attackers must provision independent clock domains and real-time pacing per identity, raising per-sybil cost from near-zero to sustained compute and latency overhead.
